topic: Improving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for question answering

selected_papers.title: ChunkRank: Relevance-Weighted Passage Selection for RAG
selected_papers.abstract: We propose ChunkRank, a lightweight reranking step that scores retrieved passages by relevance to the query before they are shown to a generation model. On two short-context QA benchmarks, ChunkRank improves answer accuracy over a standard top-k retrieval baseline, with a small added latency cost from the reranking step. All experiments use single-hop, English-language questions.

selected_papers.title: LongMem: Compressive Memory for Multi-Hop Retrieval
selected_papers.abstract: LongMem introduces a compressive memory module that lets a retrieval system summarize and reuse information across multiple retrieval hops instead of re-retrieving from scratch each time. On a multi-hop QA benchmark, LongMem improves accuracy over single-hop retrieval baselines, but adds noticeably higher inference latency due to the memory compression step. Evaluation is limited to English-language corpora.

selected_papers.title: CiteGuard: Faithfulness Verification for Generated Answers
selected_papers.abstract: CiteGuard is a post-hoc verifier that checks whether each sentence of a generated answer is actually supported by the retrieved passages it cites, flagging unsupported sentences before the answer is shown to a user. Applying CiteGuard reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of an extra inference pass per answer. The verifier itself is not evaluated on multi-hop or non-English questions.

citation_correctness.label: pass
citation_correctness.rationale: The few citations present are each individually accurate -- every claim attached to [1]/[2]/[3] matches what that paper's abstract actually states. The defect in this fixture is not citation accuracy.

groundedness.label: pass
groundedness.rationale: No invented claims, numbers, or results -- every sentence is a plain, accurate restatement of its cited abstract. Deliberately contrasted with citation_and_grounding_failure.json, which is well-organized prose with bad citations; this fixture is the opposite: accurate citations with bad organization.

synthesis_quality.label: fail
synthesis_quality.rationale: Thematic Findings and Methodology Landscape both list the three papers strictly one after another ('ChunkRank ... [1]. LongMem ... [2]. CiteGuard ... [3].') with no cross-paper comparison, no shared theme identified, and no discussion of how the three relate -- exactly the paper-by-paper-summary pattern the real system prompt explicitly instructs against.

analytical_quality.label: fail
analytical_quality.rationale: Future Research Directions restates Gap Analysis's three gaps almost verbatim ('do not evaluate multilingual settings' -> 'should address multilingual settings') without turning any of them into a concrete, actionable proposal -- violating the diagnostic-vs-prescriptive distinction Gap Analysis and Future Research Directions are supposed to maintain.

template_fit.label: fail
template_fit.rationale: R6C.3a (after run_id 6 exposed this as stale): template fit includes depth and tone, not tone alone -- the report substantially under-explains (a bare one-sentence-per-paper listing) and lacks the analytical depth the Analytical template requires, independent of the separate coherence/synthesis repetition defects.

coherence.label: fail
coherence.rationale: The Conclusion repeats the Executive Summary's opening sentence almost verbatim ('This review covers/covered reranking, compressive memory, and post-hoc verification as three ways to improve retrieval-augmented generation'), and Thematic Findings and Methodology Landscape independently restate the same three one-fact-per-paper statements without adding new information between the two sections.

source_balance.label: pass
source_balance.rationale: Each of the three papers is cited exactly once in each of the three sections that cite anything at all -- perfectly even distribution. Included deliberately to show source_balance is independent of synthesis_quality: this report is balanced AND badly synthesized at the same time.

notes: Reuses the same 3 synthetic papers as good_analytical.json so a reviewer can directly compare a well-synthesized report and a paper-by-paper-listing report built from identical evidence. No web article included (deliberately -- this fixture isn't testing source_balance or web/paper mixing). Structurally valid: sequential references 1-3, no orphans, no leaked markers, no missing/empty sections. Every defect here is a synthesis/analytical/coherence failure an LLM judge must catch; none of it is detectable by the R6 deterministic gate.
